entries.rationale: The repository has no git remote, so nothing states a name. The app is a status board: the backend stores status checks and the frontend lists them. This name goes into every label, the namespace, the Ingress and the ArgoCD application, so it is worth getting right once.
One hostname serves both routes: the frontend at / and the API at /api. Answering this first is what makes the frontend's baked API base answerable, because the two are the same origin.

The bundle computes its API base as `${REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api`. With the frontend and the API on one hostname, the empty string makes that a same-origin /api call, which works on any host the bundle is served from and needs no rebuild if the hostname later changes.

A team leaving a hosted platform for a compliance requirement is not usually looking to start operating a database. Managed keeps backups and failover someone else's problem, and it makes the version question moot.
Where the built images are pushed. The overlay's image transform is unusable until this is a real path.
The generated tree is rooted in the application repository, because the Dockerfiles have to COPY application source. So ArgoCD watches that same repository.
ingress-nginx is the most common controller and the one the generated path rules assume when they order /api before /.
